summary: Describes an optional change to TCP slow-start for connections with very large congestion windows. Normal slow-start can add thousands of segments in a round trip, causing massive losses, so this limits the growth. It is experimental.

eli5.summary: A car speeding up faster and faster eventually crashes. This tells very fast connections to ease up gently instead of doubling speed every time.

questions: tcp slow start with large windows
subtitle: Easing into speed for high-capacity TCP connections

tldr.problem: TCP's standard slow-start can double the congestion window every round-trip time. For modern high-speed connections with windows of thousands of segments, this causes the sender to inject thousands of packets at once, leading to massive losses and retransmission timeouts.
tldr.mechanism: Limited Slow-Start introduces a new parameter (max_ssthresh) that caps how much the congestion window grows per round-trip time when the window exceeds this threshold, slowing the exponential growth into a more gradual increase.
tldr.outcome: The sender reaches a target window more slowly but with far fewer packet losses and retransmission timeouts, improving overall throughput and reducing impact on other traffic sharing the link.

today: RFC 3742 is an Experimental specification providing guidance for TCP implementations on high-speed or long-distance links. It has not been obsoleted and remains a useful reference for connection flow control optimization.

sections.title: The Slow-Start Problem
sections.content:
TCP slow-start is designed to probe the network's available capacity without overwhelming it. In the standard algorithm, the sender increases the congestion window by one Maximum Segment Size (MSS) for every acknowledgement received, effectively doubling the window each round-trip time. This aggressive growth works well for typical connections, but for high-speed long-distance links or modern data centers, the congestion window can grow to thousands of segments.

When the window reaches such sizes, doubling it in one round-trip time means injecting thousands of new packets into the network. Even well-tuned router queues cannot absorb such a burst without dropping many packets. The result is often counterproductive: instead of reaching a high sending rate, the sender experiences massive loss, triggering retransmission timeouts, and ends up at a very small congestion window in congestion avoidance mode. Recovery takes many round-trip times.
sections.eli5: If you double your speed every second, you go from walking to crashing into a wall very quickly. That is not smart for getting there faster.

sections.title: The Limited Slow-Start Mechanism
sections.content:
Limited Slow-Start introduces a parameter max_ssthresh, recommended to be set to 100 MSS. The algorithm proceeds in two phases: when the congestion window is at or below max_ssthresh, the sender uses standard slow-start, increasing the window by one MSS per ACK. When the window exceeds max_ssthresh, the sender enters Limited Slow-Start mode.

In Limited Slow-Start mode, the window growth is capped so that the maximum increase per round-trip time is max_ssthresh / 2 segments. For each arriving ACK, the sender increments the window by int(MSS / K), where K = int(cwnd / (0.5 * max_ssthresh)). This formula ensures that as the window grows larger, the increments per ACK shrink inversely, keeping the total growth per RTT bounded.
sections.eli5: Instead of doubling speed every time, shift to adding a tiny bit each time. The bigger you get, the tinier the increments.

sections.title: Growth Rates and Performance
sections.content:
With Limited Slow-Start set to max_ssthresh = 100 MSS, it takes approximately log(100) ≈ 7 round-trip times to reach 100 MSS, just like standard slow-start. Beyond that, reaching a window of 83,000 packets requires about 836 round-trip times instead of just 16 without Limited Slow-Start (assuming no losses).

The key advantage is queue management: the transient queue during standard slow-start reaching 83,000 packets would exceed 32,000 packets. With Limited Slow-Start, the largest transient queue stays around 100 packets. This massive reduction in buffering prevents the large packet drops that trigger timeouts. The result is fewer retransmissions and overall better performance even though it takes longer to reach full speed.
sections.eli5: Getting to high speed takes longer, but you do not crash into a wall of dropped packets halfway there.

sections.title: Deployment and Results
sections.content:
Implementation in Linux 2.4.16 Web100 kernel demonstrated improved performance for TCP connections using Limited Slow-Start compared to standard slow-start. Experiments showed that the algorithm works well with different values of max_ssthresh, though the recommended value of 100 MSS provides a good balance.

Limited Slow-Start is orthogonal to other TCP improvements and can be deployed alongside rate-based pacing, Appropriate Byte Counting, and other congestion control enhancements. The mechanism introduces no new options or packet overhead; it is a purely local sender-side change to the slow-start algorithm.
sections.eli5: Tests showed the gentler approach actually works better in practice, even though it is not the fastest possible way to get to high speed.

sections.title: Related Proposals
sections.content:
Several research directions aim to improve slow-start for high-speed connections. TCP Vegas and other schemes monitor available bandwidth by observing RTT changes to exit slow-start early. History-based approaches initialize the congestion window based on information from previous connections to the same destination. Rate-based pacing spreads packet transmissions over time rather than sending them in bursts, and could be combined with Limited Slow-Start for further improvement.

The RFC notes that Limited Slow-Start is also orthogonal to Appropriate Byte Counting (RFC 3465), which increases the window based on bytes acknowledged rather than the number of ACKs. Each approach addresses different aspects of slow-start behavior, and they can coexist in a single implementation.
sections.eli5: Other ideas exist for improving slow-start, and this one can be used with most of them.
